pages.api:
# API reference

> The readings, the report, the store vector, the export endpoints and the settings.

## Reading `detections/<name>` (default `vis0`)

`detections.v1`, class `reading`: `source_id`, `node_id`, `t_ns` (the frame's), `seq`, `frame_hash` (BLAKE3 of the frame), `model`, `boxes` (at most 64): each `label`, `score` (0..1; 1.0 when the model gave none) and `bbox` `[x, y, w, h]` normalized to the frame.

## Call made

`svc.infer/<service>` with `infer.v1`: `model`, `priority`, `max_tokens`, `system`, `text`, `image_blob` (the frame's `blob.v1` handle).

## Reading `telemetry/<name>`

`telemetry.v1`: `frames.seen`, `frames.asked`, `detections`, `boxes`, `failures`, `latency.mean` (ms), `bus.connected`.

## stdout

`{"frame": "...", "labels": [...]}` per frame looked at, then one report per interval:

| Field | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `status` | string | `ok`, `no_source`, `simulate`, `replay` |
| `provenance` | string | `MEASURED`, `SYNTHETIC` or `REPLAY` |
| `model`, `brain` | string | the alias; `svc.infer/<service>` or `synthetic` |
| `frames_seen`, `frames_asked`, `answers`, `detections_published` | numbers | since start |
| `boxes`, `labels_only_boxes` | numbers | boxes published; those that cover the whole frame |
| `unusable_frames`, `unparsed_answers`, `failures` | numbers | |
| `replaced_while_busy`, `throttled` | numbers | frames skipped for a newer one; frames skipped for the rate limit |
| `mean_latency_ms` | number | per answered frame |
| `last_labels`, `last_error` | array, string/null | |
| `bus` | object | `connected`, `subscribed`, `published`, `error` |

## Store vector (id 37)

Eight floats; a source that is absent is **-1**.

| Slot | Name |
|---|---|
| 0 | `frames_seen` |
| 1 | `frames_asked` |
| 2 | `published` |
| 3 | `boxes` |
| 4 | `mean_latency_ms` |
| 5 | `failures` |
| 6 | `replaced` |
| 7 | `bus_connected` |

## Export (`http://127.0.0.1:8071`, continuous mode)

`/status`, `/raw`, `/history`, `/guide`, `/healthz`.

## Settings

`--interval`, `--window`, `--model`, `--service`, `--source`, `--name`, `--min-interval-ms`, `--priority`, `--max-tokens`, `--timeout-s`, `--api-bind`, `--replay`, `--simulate`.
pages.model:
# The model

> What the vision model is asked, and what comes back.

The cog calls `svc.infer/<service>` (default `venq-npu`) with an `infer.v1` request:

- `model`: the **Model** alias (default `qwen3-vl-4b`), `priority` 3, up to **Answer length** tokens;
- `image_blob`: the frame's `blob.v1` handle, copied from the camera's reading. The handle travelling in the call is what lets the service read the frame;
- `system` and `text`: a fixed instruction.

## The instruction

> You are the vision system of a small embedded board. You are shown one camera frame. Reply with only a JSON array of the objects you can see. Each item is {"label": a short noun, "bbox": [x, y, w, h], "score": 0 to 1}. x, y, w, h are fractions of the frame width and height, from the top left corner. Give at most 10 items. If you see nothing clear, reply [].

## How the answer is read

The first JSON array in the reply is used (inside a code fence, after prose, or under a `detections` / `objects` key). Each item needs a `label`. A `bbox` of four numbers inside the frame is kept (clamped to stay inside); anything else makes the box the whole frame. A missing score is 1.0, meaning not measured. An empty list is a frame with no objects and is published as such; a reply with no list is counted as unparsed and nothing is published.
pages.setup:
# Set up

> Run it from a shell, then place it on the node.

## From a shell

```
cog-vision-detect --once --simulate                     # one canned frame, canned answer
cog-vision-detect --once --replay frames.jsonl          # frame-ref bodies to the real service
cog-vision-detect                                       # continuous; watches video.frame-ref/cam0
```

Each frame looked at is printed as `{"frame": ..., "labels": [...]}` and, with a broker, published as a detection.

## Placed on a node

Place `vision-detect` in the same project as `camera` and `npu-infer`. Its `cog.toml` declares the inputs `video.frame-ref` and `svc.infer` and the outputs `detections` and `telemetry`. It declares no device.
pages.start:
# Start here

> Say what is in front of the camera, without moving pixels around.

`vision-detect` reads the frame announcements of the `camera` cog. Each announcement carries a handle to the JPEG in the node's blob store. The cog passes that handle, not the picture, to the node's vision model, asks for a list of the objects it sees, and publishes the list as `detections/vis0` (`detections.v1`).

## The short path

1. **Run `camera`** with the blob store on (the default). → see its guide
2. **Have the inference service** serving a vision model. → see **The model**
3. **Try it without either.** `cog-vision-detect --once --simulate` looks at one canned frame and prints two canned objects.
4. **Place it** with `camera` and `npu-infer` in one project. → see **Set up**

## How the signal flows

```diagram
flow
```

## Honest limits

- The model describes; it does not measure. A vision-language model's boxes are approximate and its scores are its own claim, not a calibrated probability. When it gives a label with no usable box, the detection covers the whole frame (`[0, 0, 1, 1]`); the report counts those as `labels_only_boxes`. A detector model (YOLOX on the NPU) would give real boxes and scores; the service does not run one yet.
- A vision model takes seconds per frame, so the cog looks at about one frame every few seconds, whatever the camera's rate. Newer frames replace older waiting ones.
- The frame's bytes live in the blob store only for the camera's frame lifetime (10 s by default). A slow model on a busy NPU can miss it; the report counts `unusable_frames`.
- It needs the service to accept an image by handle (`image_blob` on `infer.v1`). Until `npu-infer` does, calls are refused and counted as `failures`.
pages.troubleshoot:
# Troubleshoot

> What each failure looks like and what to do.

## `unusable_frames` grows

`last_error` says why: `no blob handle in the reading` means `camera` runs with **No blob store** or without a broker; `the frame's blob has expired` means the model took longer than the frame lifetime. Raise the camera's **Frame lifetime**.

## `failures` grows

| `last_error` starts with | Meaning | Do this |
|---|---|---|
| `unavailable` | nobody serves `svc.infer/<service>` | place `npu-infer` |
| `service_error` | the service refused the request, for example it does not take `image_blob` yet or the model is unknown | the message says |
| `timeout` | queue or model load took longer than **Call timeout** | raise it |
| `unauthorized` | the cog was placed without its `svc.infer` input | place the package again |

## `unparsed_answers` grows

The model replied in prose. Try a larger model, or read `last_error` for the start of what it said.

## Boxes are all `[0, 0, 1, 1]`

The model gives labels without boxes (`labels_only_boxes` is high). That is the model's limit; see the limits on the first page.

## No frames at all

`frames_seen` is zero: **Camera source** does not match the camera's source id, or the camera is not publishing.

toml:
# Sensor guide for vision-detect (WeftOS ADR-104 sensor-guide format, schema 1).
# Pages are Markdown files next to this one (guide/<page>.md).

schema = 1
title = "Finding objects in camera frames"
sensor = "Frames from the camera cog, a vision model on the node"
cog = "vision-detect"
cog_version = "0.1.0"
medical = false
pages = ["start", "model", "setup", "troubleshoot", "api"]

# Checklist step ids the companion app links to a page.
[links]
cog_installed = "setup"
cog_running = "setup"
model = "model"
no_source = "troubleshoot"

# Signal flow, left to right.
[[flow]]
name = "video.frame-ref/cam0"
detail = "hash, size, blob handle"

[[flow]]
name = "vision-detect cog"
detail = "newest frame, rate limit"

[[flow]]
name = "svc.infer"
detail = "vision model, handle in the call"

[[flow]]
name = "detections/vis0"
detail = "labels and boxes"
